title: Building agent memory on Elasticsearch
description: Persistent, multi-tenant agent memory backed by Elasticsearch: three indices, hybrid recall with RRF and a cross-encoder reranker, supersession, decay, and DLS isolation, with empirical numbers from a QA-style eval.
author: noam-schwartz
blog_aim: Show how to build persistent agent memory on Elasticsearch end-to-end: three indices per memory lifecycle, hybrid RRF + reranker retrieval, supersession for contradictions, time-decay and use-count scoring, DLS for per-user isolation, and MCP for agent-agnostic access. Reader should leave able to make architecture decisions for their own agent's memory layer.
topic_scope: In scope: three-bucket memory model, hybrid recall pipeline (RRF + over-fetch + cross-encoder reranker), same-turn write visibility, supersession-not-deletion, time-decay scoring, per-user DLS isolation, catalog federation, MCP endpoint, QA-style retrieval eval. Out of scope: agent framework comparisons, chat UI build, production-scale tuning beyond the corpus probed.
target_audience: Engineers building agents that need long-term memory (search engineers, platform engineers, ML/RAG developers comfortable with Elasticsearch concepts). Secondary: technical leaders evaluating Elasticsearch as an agent memory layer.
success_criteria: Reader can decide whether three memory shapes fits their workload, reproduce the RRF + over-fetch + reranker pipeline shape, recognise supersession-not-deletion, understand DLS-as-architecture vs backend-filter trade-offs on Serverless, and run the linked demo if curious.
